_notes: THE FLIGHT LOOP, ALONE. This is one quarter of what prismatic_orb_water.json
cut as a single 15-frame sequence: that recipe stitched a travelling ball and a
contact burst into one timeline, which is one drawing per cast and therefore one
thing on screen. The layered presentation plays the core, its wake, its shed and
its splash as four independent layers, so each needs its own folder with its own
provenance. The combined recipe stays on disk, unplayed, as the baseline the
layered version is measured against.
SIX CELLS, IN ORDER, NOTHING COMPOSED. water_core_6f.png is already an authored
six-frame loop of internal motion (the sources' own README), and the 1536x1024
sheet divides exactly into 512px cells -- the one sheet of the four that does.
No rects, no canvas, no scale steps.
DELIVERED WITH ITS OWN ALPHA, so keyed is false and nothing is re-keyed from
luminance. Measured on the cut cells: alpha is effectively binary -- 29% of every
cell above 128 and 0% between 8 and 128 -- so the README's 'soft blue halo' is
drawn in RGB against a hard alpha edge rather than as a falloff. The cell edges
carry alpha 0-1, so there is no rectangle to read against the dark stage: the
halo stops well inside the cell.
PLAYED AS A LOOP by the layer that owns it (until: loop, fps 24 over a 0.25s
flight is exactly one revolution), which is what makes the f5->f0 seam a question
at all. The seam is a playback decision and lives in skills.json, not here: the
recipe's job is that the six cells arrive uncomposed and in order.
